messages.author: 866c5198d7460eae
messages.subject: Multiple libraries from vcftools
parts:
Hi everyone,

I have genotype data (from ddRADseq of wild, F1, and F2 individuals) across three libraries that I want to concatenate for use in R/qtl. The cleanup (radtag processing, demultiplexing, removing PCR duplicates, alignment, etc.) was done by a collaborator, resulting in three separate .vcf files (one for each library). After my own quality filtering, I output each library to a 012 file (all through vcftools) and loaded those files into R to assemble data frames that would be usable in R/qtl. However, I'm not able to merge/join these data frames to analyze together due to different dimensions and loss of information (eg/ ‘marker 2’ in Lib01 is groupI 33579, whereas ‘marker 2’ in Lib02 is groupI 71336, and ‘marker 2’ in Lib 03 is groupI 149468).

This is my first stab at dealing with these data and I'm sure there are lots of people who have dealt with this before, I'm just having a hard time finding some direction for next steps. Do I need to go back to the original raw files and concatenate there, or are there steps I can take to do this with the processed data? Any and all advice or feedback would be greatly appreciated!

Cheers,

Sara

messages.author: 9af7c0e584af0222
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Multiple libraries from vcftools
parts: Better you paste three datasets one by one (all three datasets in a single panel). Then do the filtering. Don't do the filtering for an individual library otherwise, finally the number won't be matched.

messages.author: 9892f9c35b87e857
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Multiple libraries from vcftools
parts:
Hello Sara:

There are some tools in GATK or Picard tools, try the following links for suggestion.

https://gatkforums.broadinstitute.org/gatk/discussion/53/combining-variants-from-different-files-into-one

There are MergeVcfs, GatherVcfs in Picard, CatVariants, CombineVariants in GATK.

These functions should consider if the samples are the same across vcfs, or the variants are the same across vcfs.

Maybe you can try CombineVariants first! But don’t forget to sort the vcfs before concatenate.

Don’t forget to consider the genotype quality which may depend on read depth in ddRAD library result.


Hope these will help… 

Chun San

Hello~

Sorry for the members of discussion group, the following instructions seem to be GATK channel… sorry for Mr. Broman...

The GATK4 is quite different from GATK3, but the function we use is just a small part of it, so I think go bake a little to GATK3 just fine.

GATK3 still can be found on the website, both of the .jar software and the User guide page which need to switch back to GATK3 docs manually. The orange bottom on the top left of the user guide page.

Here is the GATK3:

GATK website > Download > Archived versions: then you can see GATK 2-3 bottom and click.

The unzip the tar.bz2 file, then GATK is ready to use. It’s lucky to hear you know how to use bcftools, it means you can manage linux system yourself.

Take a look for installation for GATK, only at the GATK part will be fine!

https://software.broadinstitute.org/gatk/documentation/article?id=7098

After you install JAVA suitable for GATK3, and run the help page, then you can start the CombineVariants function.

I think GATK is quite easy to use, as long as the JAVA version is correct.

Please feel free if you still sock at some part of GATK.

I think while we move to higher demential genotype data, especially genotyping with NGS technology.

The less missing rate (<10%) and higher genotype quality or variant quality will vary help for linkage map construction.

The more confidence for the markers, the more stable of the map, then r/qtl will give you the more solid QTL mapping result.

Please take some times with your genotype table, it will help a lot.

By the way, the r/qtl2 is release! And it will suit for high dimensional data!

Still, I’m sorry for the long discussion before the r/qtl start! Hope you won’t mind!

Chun San

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Multiple libraries from vcftools
parts:
On Tue, Dec 04, 2018 at 10:05:11AM -0800, sjswu...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi everyone,
>
> I have genotype data (from ddRADseq of wild, F1, and F2 individuals) across three libraries that I want to concatenate for use in R/qtl. The cleanup (radtag processing, demultiplexing, removing PCR duplicates, alignment, etc.) was done by a collaborator, resulting in three separate .vcf files (one for each library). After my own quality filtering, I output each library to a 012 file (all through vcftools) and loaded those files into R to assemble data frames that would be usable in R/qtl. However, I'm not able to merge/join these data frames to analyze together due to different dimensions and loss of information (eg/ ‘marker 2’ in Lib01 is groupI 33579, whereas ‘marker 2’ in Lib02 is groupI 71336, and ‘marker 2’ in Lib 03 is groupI 149468).

I think you need more power than vcftools offers. I find
https://github.com/pjotrp/bioruby-vcf to be a useful tool for
pre-processed (command line) filtering and arranging of data. I wrote
the tool for that very reason. Many examples in README and ./doc

There are other tools.

Alternatively load the raw VCF data into R and write R-code to
re-organize it.

> This is my first stab at dealing with these data and I'm sure there are lots of people who have dealt with this before, I'm just having a hard time finding some direction for next steps. Do I need to go back to the original raw files and concatenate there, or are there steps I can take to do this with the processed data? Any and all advice or feedback would be greatly appreciated!

Dealing with VCF files to be my bread and butter at some point. It is
ugly.

Pj.
